canonical_form: sha256 over these exact bytes: the JSON object {date, prev_manifest_hash, files} with keys in that literal order, serialized with compact separators (no space after ',' or ':'); each file object with keys in the order path, sha256, bytes, standing; non-ASCII emitted as raw UTF-8 and NEVER \u-escaped (Python's json.dumps defaults to ensure_ascii=True and will fail here); no trailing newline. File order is depth-first pre-order: within each directory, entries are sorted by the UTF-8 BYTES of the entry name, and a directory's contents are emitted at that directory's own sorted position. Two traps: this is NOT a bytewise sort of the full path strings, which would place 'sub.txt' before 'sub/c.txt' since '.' (0x2E) precedes '/' (0x2F); and it is NOT JavaScript's default string compare, which orders UTF-16 code units and puts U+10000 before U+FFFD where UTF-8 bytes put U+FFFD first.
fixture_covers: compact separators — a ', ' or ': ' build fails on every entry
non-ASCII in a FILENAME (é.txt) — file CONTENT is hashed to hex and never reaches the payload, so content alone cannot test this
directory-vs-sibling-file ordering (sub/ against sub.txt) — separates depth-first traversal from a full-path bytewise sort
supplementary-plane ordering (U+FFFD against U+10000) — separates a UTF-8 byte compare from a UTF-16 code-unit compare
